thread:
Incident Bot: PagerDuty ALERT: HIGH - host-gpu-211 (us-west-2a) unreachable, kubelet NotReady, possible kernel oops. PD:PD-8341
Ops Oncall Bot: page fired -> escalation policy: infra-gpu / 2min / pagerduty
Alice Chen: acked the page, I'm looking now.
Marco Rivera: oncall? I can take network checks if needed.
Alice Chen: thanks. first quick checks: kubectl shows node NotReady and taints. ssh to 10.12.45.211 times out.
Jaya Patel: logging: last syslog snippet from node shows repeated block device errors then soft lockup. pastebin: https://paste.redwood.local/4f3b
Emma Lopez: can you paste kernel log tail?
Alice Chen: kernel tail: ```
[ 12345.678901] nvme0: I/O 0 QID 0 timeout, status:0x5
[ 12345.679012] blk_update_request: I/O error, dev nvme0n1, sector 123456789
[ 12345.679123] Kernel panic - not syncing: hung_task: blocked for more than 120 seconds
```
Ops Oncall Bot: PagerDuty note: incident-bot set severity=high, auto-escalate in 2m if not acked by lead.
Marco Rivera: that looks like disk/driver-level failure on the host. Could be NVMe firmware hang. Are GPU processes stuck?
Alice Chen: yes, container processes on that node are in D state when last polled. Kubernetes shows pods stuck on that node; new pods are being scheduled to other nodes but eviction not completed.
Jaya Patel: customer impact check: routing rules show model shard for customer:acme-inc had ~8% of requests hitting that rack. Most requests routed to fallback model in other region automatically. So partial degradation for a small set of customers. No full outage.
Emma Lopez: posting to status: "Partial impact to inference latency for a subset of customers in us-west-2. Automatic fallbacks active; no customer-facing downtime reported yet." Will update.
Alice Chen: mitigation plan: 1) cordon node (k8s) 2) drain with force to move remaining pods 3) mark host for maintenance and trigger host remediation (reboot + nvme controller reset) 4) if reboots fail, remove from pool and provision replacement.
Marco Rivera: agree. I'll try a soft nvme reset via IPMI/hostconsole if we get serial access. If that fails, we should reprovision host from spare pool.
Jaya Patel: going to kick off drain now: `kubectl cordon host-gpu-211 && kubectl drain host-gpu-211 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --force`
Alice Chen: drain started. some pods evicting. seeing 12/14 pods reschedule.
Ops Oncall Bot: Note: autoscaler triggered to spin up 2 burst instances for capacity.
Emma Lopez: status page updated with mitigation steps. tagging #customers-impact and support.
Alice Chen: attempted ssh again via console -> serial shows kernel oops continuing, but we got IPMI console logs: nvme firmware reported multiple resets, host not responding to kernel threads. Reboot attempt initiated (soft).
Marco Rivera: if soft reboot doesn't clear nvme state, do hard power cycle. I'll stand by for IPMI confirmation.
Alice Chen: soft reboot failed; host didn't come back. initiating hard power cycle now.
Jaya Patel: after power cycle host came up to grub but then hangs later in kernel init. suspect persistent hardware fault.
Emma Lopez: notifying support+sales for customers with heavy usage on that rack. Drafting email with mitigation summary.
Ops Oncall Bot: escalation timer: 10m -> if node not recovered, escalate to infra-leads.
Alice Chen: decision: remove host from pool and reprovision replacement from spare images. Starting reprovision job.
Marco Rivera: assigning myself to reprovision image and nvme diagnostics on new host.
Jaya Patel: handing off active incident to SRE Rotation for post-reprovision follow-ups and host postmortem. @SRE Rotation please ack and take over.
SRE Rotation: acked, taking over. Will coordinate postmortem and next steps including firmware rollout to remaining hosts in that rack.
Emma Lopez: final customer impact note: "Impact: small subset of inference requests experienced higher latency or retries for ~27 minutes while traffic shifted. Root cause: NVMe device failure causing kernel hang on GPU host. Remediation: host removed and reprovisioned; we will run nvme firmware audit and add monitoring for persistent I/O error metrics."
Alice Chen: closing the page after reprovision completes. leaving action items: - run nvme firmware audit across rack - add k8s probe to detect kernel oops earlier - update runbook with forced power-cycle steps and reprovision checklist.
SRE Rotation: capturing action items in incident tracker PD-8341 and scheduling postmortem sync.
Incident Bot: PagerDuty: incident acknowledged and escalations suspended.
Alice Chen: thanks team. I'll follow up on postmortem notes later today. :thumbsup:
